title: What Art Do You Love?
subtitle: 14 artworks. 14 quick decisions. Discover the art you're naturally drawn to.

categories.name: Abstract
categories.description: You're drawn to art that doesn't necessarily tell you exactly what to see. Abstract art uses colour, shape, texture and movement to create an emotional or visual experience rather than simply representing the world as it appears. You may be drawn to artwork that makes you feel something before you understand it.

categories.name: Portraiture
categories.description: You're drawn to the human face — the way a single expression can hold an entire story. Portraiture captures presence: a gaze, a gesture, the quiet particulars of a real person, rendered so closely you feel you could know them. You may be drawn to artwork that feels almost like eye contact.

categories.name: Realism
categories.description: You're drawn to art that shows life exactly as it is — the everyday, the unglamorous, the true. Realism finds dignity and detail in ordinary people and ordinary moments, without softening or idealising them. You may be drawn to artwork that feels honest before it feels beautiful.

categories.name: Landscape
categories.description: You're drawn to the natural world — sky, sea, mountain, mist. Landscape art captures scale and atmosphere, the feeling of standing somewhere vast and being reminded how small you are. You may be drawn to artwork that makes you want to breathe a little slower.

categories.name: Classical
categories.description: You're drawn to art with weight and history — technique that took a lifetime to master, subjects drawn from myth and the ideals of the past. Classical art rewards close looking: composition, symbolism, the sheer skill of the hand. You may be drawn to artwork that feels timeless rather than of-the-moment.

categories.name: Modern / Contemporary
categories.description: You're drawn to art that broke the rules to make new ones. Modern art traded convention for experimentation — new colour, new form, new ways of seeing the everyday world. You may be drawn to artwork that still feels like it's asking a question.

categories.name: Social Commentary
categories.description: You're drawn to art with something to say. Social commentary uses image to hold up a mirror — to injustice, to power, to the lives of people history usually overlooks. You may be drawn to artwork that unsettles you a little, on purpose.
